rows.decision: The page is a list on the left, grouped by service, and the chosen connection's details on the right.
Integrations is renamed Connections in the nav, with a plug icon, and the Slack alert login (Bidspoke Alerts) and the HTTP services are listed as connections.
A Needs attention group comes first, holding every connection with a problem, each with its service and what is wrong under its name; the rest are grouped by service, alphabetical.
Section headings in the list are dark, normal case, 14px semibold, with a line above each section. This is for the Connections page only, not a rule for other lists.
The detail panel has three tabs: Connection, Used by (n), History.
Reconnect and Replace are quiet buttons under the facts; Remove is set apart in its own row at the bottom of the panel.
A problem shows as a shaded notice at the top of the Connection tab: when it began and its cause, its effect, a grey fix line, and a blue Reconnect inside it; the status under the name reads in red.

On the canvas, a step's Connection field is the app's dropdown with the chosen connection's name, with only "Acts as <who>" under it; nothing about status on a healthy day. A connection with a problem adds one red line, "Needs reconnecting on the Connections page", its last two words a dark underlined link to that page.
rows.detail: docs/design/connections-step-form.html and its checks (connections-step-form.checks.js), which hold the step form frames

rows.decision: While a workflow uses the connection, Remove is greyed out, its row reads "Cannot be removed while a workflow uses it.", and a plain "Used by:" list of the workflows sits under the row, with no button.

Google mailboxes and drives: an entry at the top of the Google section; choosing it shows in the panel the heading, a sentence whose term "domain wide delegation" carries its one sentence explanation, one row per entry with address, kind, "Added by <who>, <date>" and Remove on one line, and an add box with Add.
Add connection is the blue button at the top right of the page, always there once the list has loaded; it opens the form in the right panel in place of the details, with nothing chosen in the list.

The service is chosen from a grid of tiles in two columns, each the service's name and one line of what it connects. The tiles come from the service catalogue, so a service appears once its catalogue entry ships.
While saving, Save greys out and a line under the buttons shows a spinner, what is happening and the seconds counting.
A failed save turns the same line red: what failed, that nothing was saved, and what to do; Save is ready again.

Salesforce's fields are Name, Org, Client id and Client secret (masked). Org is a dropdown of the orgs Bidspoke knows, by name, with the address in a grey line under it, and Another org last. Choosing Another org makes Org a box the new org's address is typed into, and its menu offers "Use <address> as a new org". Who it acts as is read from Salesforce when the login is checked, never typed.

Google's fields are Name, then two choice cards, "A company mailbox or drive" (From the company list) and "My own Google account" (Signed in as you); the company card shows a dropdown of the company list.
For your own Google account, Google's own white Sign in with Google button, with its logo, replaces Save.
After a save, the new connection opens in the panel and is chosen in the list, with no message.
Reconnect opens a dialog "Reconnect <name>" with the client id kept and a New client secret field, Save and Cancel. Its title is 20px, the size of every dialog's title.

Replace opens a dialog "Replace <name>" with a Replace with dropdown, the workflows listed and ticked under "In these workflows", "Each ticked workflow gets a new version with <replacement>.", and a red "Replace in <n> workflows" and Cancel. Its title is 20px, the size of every dialog's title.

Removing a connection no workflow uses: Remove is ready, and it opens a dialog "Remove <name>?" saying "Its login is deleted from Bidspoke and cannot be brought back.", with Cancel and a red Remove. Its title is 20px, the size of every dialog's title.
When login checks are not answering, a strip at the top says so and gives the time of the last statuses, with Try again; the last known statuses stay shown, Needs attention included.
When the list did not load, one card across the page says so, with Try again, and Add connection is hidden until it loads.
Blue is for buttons only; links are dark and underlined.
Red is only for something genuinely wrong, or for the button that destroys.
Every fact once per screen.
No line of text ends with a single word on its own line; reword or rebalance it. A rule for all of Bidspoke's copy, made by Dan on 2026-10-20 in these rounds.
An open dropdown's highlighted row is pale grey (#F1EFEA) behind dark text; a rule for every dropdown.
Adding to the Google list starts with a choice between Mailbox and Shared drive, the app's own choice group, Mailbox chosen; a mailbox is then one box, Mailbox address, with Add beside it.
A shared drive is added by pasting its whole Google Drive address; the page reads the drive's ID out of it and never shows the ID back.
The drive's address has a line of its own, and its name, Drive name, shown on this list, sits on the line under it with Add at the end.
A working line's spinner is as tall as the capital letters and level with them, in every working line in the app.

An org with no limit set on its Salesforce calls is refused in Dan's words: "Bidspoke has no limit set yet on how many Salesforce calls its workflows may make to <org address>, so it cannot connect to that org. Nothing was saved. Ask Dan to set a limit for this org, then save again."
A dropdown's open menu sits over what is below it, never pushing the page down; the Org menu as every other.
Every dialog's title is 20px, drawn by the app's one title rule.
On a highlighted row, an option's grey second line is a darker grey (#666D7E) so it stays readable; every other grey hint is unchanged.
rows.detail: apps/web/src/lib/__guards__/dropdown-highlight-guard.test.ts, which holds the second line on every dropdown's highlighted row to #666D7E and measures it at 4.5 to 1 or more on the highlight. No frame draws a highlighted option with a second line: the one open menu, on add-salesforce-new-org, offers only Use <address> as a new org.
